newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh call money rates jump to 30-40 percent.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh call money rates jump to 30-40 percent.

text.p: Bangladesh's interbank call money rates jumped to 30-40 percent from 8.0-10 percent on a sudden liquidity crunch due to heavy withdrawals ahead of the Moslem Eid al-Adha festival, dealers said.
"This is not unusual before the Eid al-Adha festival. The interbank call money rate may have jumped but it does not indicate any liquidity crisis, said one central bank official.
Officials with commercial banks said the market had nearly 10 billion taka in excess liquidity, which was in the form of loanable funds.

Officials said call money rates jumped after leather sector companies rushed for funds to buy hides and skins of cows and goats to be slaughtered during the three-day Eid festival beginning on Thursday.
Market sources said nearly 20 million cows and goats are slaughtered for the feast every year in Bangladesh.
A private bank borrowed 100 million taka at 40 percent from another private bank, said one senior bank official.
Bank officials said liquidity had also dried up after commercial banks paid 1.68 billion taka to the central bank for treasury bills.
